primary_meaning: the wicked/ungodly (or worthless people) who are separated from the righteous and destined for judgment or destruction

alternatives.meaning: anything worthless, empty, or transient that is easily discarded or scattered
basis: general agricultural imagery in wisdom literature and prophets (e.g., Job 13:25; Isaiah 29:5; 41:15)

alternatives.meaning: false or hypocritical believers / empty profession of faith (as opposed to genuine fruit)
basis: extension of the wheat-and-chaff winnowing motif in preaching on Matthew 3:12 / Luke 3:17

notes: Standard Christian and Jewish interpretive tradition treats chaff almost exclusively via the threshing/winnowing metaphor as the negative counterpart to wheat/grain; the judgment/destruction sense is the dominant and near-universal application in teaching and commentaries. No major competing symbolic systems exist for the term.
